name: cuberhyk-dev-flow
description: A compact Codex lifecycle workflow plugin with orient, decision, split, exploratory review, branch, changelog, distill, and review gates.

interface.shortDescription: Init, check, orient, brainstorm, split, plan, audit, exploratory review, branch, changelog, and distill coding work.
interface.longDescription: cuberhyk-dev-flow provides twelve focused Codex skills. dev-brainstorm refines fuzzy ideas before planning, dev-design-system maintains durable UI rules and semantic reuse, dev-split governs large-file and module-boundary risk, and dev-plan/dev-audit include low-noise orientation gates. dev-branch executes work inside a reviewed Git branch and runs lifecycle gates plus an independent subagent-or-manual review before approval.
defaultPrompt: Use dev-init to initialize Dev Flow memory when needed.
Use dev-check to validate docs routing.
Use dev-brainstorm to refine fuzzy ideas, compare approaches, and identify decision points before planning.
Use dev-design-system after an initial UI direction is approved, or to update/check reusable UI rules.
Use dev-split to evaluate large-file, module-boundary, and code-placement risk before planning or implementation.
Use dev-plan to enter relevant context, identify decision points, and define the next task.
Use dev-audit to enter relevant context, review bounded features or workflows, and persist non-trivial findings.
Use dev-exploratory-review to map a project or scope, build a risk map, run focused probes/tests, and report realistic failures.
Use dev-branch to isolate implementation work, run lifecycle gates and an independent subagent-or-manual review, and wait for approval before commit and merge.
Use dev-orient, dev-changelog, and dev-distill standalone only when a context-only, release-note-only, or knowledge-only task needs them.
